solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Warning from worker about fight

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the worker's letters go round the fight

parts.note: a worker bee is the crossword's standard worker
a war is a fight on a grand scale

explanation.surface: A labourer cautions someone about a coming brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker is the insect, the crossword's usual worker, not a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an interjection used as a caution, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Sincere Latin

parts.note: a Latin phrase meaning in good faith, used in English for genuine or sincere

explanation.surface: A description of an honest Latin speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for in good faith is used to describe something genuine and sincere.

clue.text: Elevating device that may go over well

definitions.text: Elevating device that may go over well

parts.words: Elevating device that may go over well
parts.note: a winching drum set over a well to raise the bucket; well also hints at going down well

explanation.surface: A lifting machine that might be well received.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal drum turned by a crank to haul up loads, classically set above a well.

clue.text: European capital set up with middle man

parts.note: to rig is to set up equipment, or a fixed result

indicators.note: middle takes the central letter of the word man

explanation.surface: A capital city arranged around a man in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Latvia, on the Baltic.

clue.text: Tea's been set out — one is missing

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of the preceding words are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: The tea is laid out, but one guest has not turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present where expected is an absentee: one person missing from the gathering.

clue.text: First-day cover?

parts.note: a philatelic term for an envelope stamped on issue day, read as what covers you on the day you are born: nothing but skin

explanation.surface: A stamp collector's envelope postmarked on a stamp's day of issue.
explanation.walkthrough: A first-day cover is a stamp collector's term; here the cover worn on your first day is bare skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular idiom for nakedness: the 'outfit' a baby wears at birth.

clue.text: A resounding comeback

parts.note: a sound that bounces back off a surface, rather than a triumphant return

explanation.surface: A sporting team's emphatic return to form.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound that comes back to the listener is literally a resounding return.

clue.text: It never rains but it pours

definitions.text: It never rains but it pours

parts.words: It never rains but it pours
parts.note: a proverb about troubles coming together, read literally as something that never rains but certainly pours

explanation.surface: The proverb that misfortunes arrive all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel for brewing that pours tea but obviously never produces rain.

clue.text: Resulted in having to go to law in the finish

indicators.note: in places the legal action inside the word for the finish

parts.note: an end is a finish
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Someone ended up having to take the matter to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the finish' reads as 'eventually', but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence; it is a synonym of resulted.

clue.text: Minority of lawyers give a 90-yr old 50% off

indicators.note: taking 50% off leaves only the front half of the word for the old person

parts.note: someone in their nineties is a nonagenarian

explanation.surface: Lawyers offer a half-price deal to a very elderly client.
explanation.walkthrough: Halving the twelve-letter word for someone aged 90 keeps its first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal language the term means the period of being under age, i.e. legal minority.

clue.text: Entrances with roguish traits

parts.note: arch means mischievous or playfully knowing
someone's ways are their habits or characteristics

explanation.surface: Someone charms their way into places with mischievous qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Arched openings serve as entrances to buildings and courtyards.

clue.text: Matches possibly made if three girls go wild

definitions.note: plural, as matches are one example of things used to start a fire

indicators.note: going wild suggests disorder, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trio of young women runs riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches are an example of the items used to kindle a fire; 'possibly' marks the example.

clue.text: Take a trip in the autumn

definitions.meaning: to trip over and tumble to the ground
the American name for the season after summer

explanation.surface: Someone goes on holiday in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means to tumble after stumbling and is also the US name for the season.

clue.text: Making a loop needs great height

parts.note: great means large

explanation.surface: A stunt pilot needs plenty of altitude to perform a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: In knot-tying, a curved slack section of rope forming a loop is called this.

clue.text: Roof party I object to

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
me is the object form of I

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a rooftop party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' sounds like a protest but means the grammatical object form of I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded vault is a type of roof over a building.

clue.text: An increase, not for the first time

parts.note: the indefinite article an, written as a
a gain is an increase

explanation.surface: Another rise, and it is not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means once more, i.e. on a repeat occasion.

clue.text: Very light, for example

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal fired from a pistol, named after its inventor, not something of little weight

explanation.surface: Something extremely weightless, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: Very here is the inventor Edward Very; a Very light is a pistol-fired signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is one kind of bright signal fired into the sky.

clue.text: Released a big eruption — it's unpleasant

indicators.note: an eruption throws things violently about, so the letters before it are scattered and re-formed

explanation.surface: A volcano lets loose a huge blast, and it is nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something not nice or agreeable; they are synonyms.

clue.text: He deals in capital investments

parts.note: capital read as head and investments as things put on, i.e. hairpieces

explanation.surface: A financier who trades in capital investments.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital means head, and to invest once meant to clothe, so headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman producing hairpieces supplies coverings for the head.

clue.text: Opening ruse designed for risky undertakings

parts.note: a vent is an opening for air

indicators.note: designed suggests something reworked, so the letters of ruse are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A cunning opening trick devised for dangerous projects.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprises involving risk, especially business ones, are called this.

clue.text: Polite assistance from public administrators

parts.note: civil means courteous
service means help given

explanation.surface: Officials offer courteous help to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of government employees who run state departments are collectively administrators of public affairs.

clue.text: I follow mother in getting degree in Indian city

indicators.note: follow means the letter I comes after the rest

parts.note: mum is mother
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Someone tags along behind mother while she earns a degree in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Indian port city formerly called Bombay.

clue.text: Leave the dance-floor to enjoy the sun?

definitions.meaning: to not take part in a dance

explanation.surface: Skip the dancing and sunbathe instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to miss a dance, and literally to be seated out of doors.

clue.text: One upper-class twit

parts.note: U is the classic label for upper-class usage
a nit is a foolish person

explanation.surface: Someone is labelled a posh fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A single whole thing counted as one is a unit.

clue.text: Love to be surrounded by unusual rich voices

indicators.note: signals that the love letter is placed inside the other letters
unusual signals the word rich appears in an altered order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic is enveloped by unusually rich singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges RICH to CHIR; 'to be surrounded by' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of singers is a collection of voices.

clue.text: Obscenity that turns stomachs

indicators.note: turns signals that the word for stomachs is read backwards

parts.note: tums is the informal word for stomachs

explanation.surface: Filth so disgusting it makes people feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or lewd material is called this; it means obscenity.

clue.text: Steal up around a wild beast

indicators.note: around means the reversed letters go round the a
in a down clue, up means the word for steal is read backwards

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Someone creeps stealthily round an untamed animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ROB to BOR; 'around' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild pig is the classic beast hunted in forests.

clue.text: Ineffective material

definitions.meaning: weak and unconvincing, as a poor excuse
a glittering fabric woven with metallic threads, spelt with an accent

explanation.surface: Cloth that does no good.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means feeble, and with an accent names a glittering metallic fabric.

clue.text: Possible setback with deliveries coming to an end

definitions.note: a participle phrase where the answer is a verb meaning to pass or subside

parts.note: a blow is a setback or misfortune
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

explanation.surface: A cricket team suffers a setback as the bowling ends.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm or row that subsides and passes is said to do this, i.e. it finishes.

clue.text: Better kind of helper

definitions.meaning: one who bets, a punter who backs a horse
a supporter who funds or helps a project

explanation.surface: An improved sort of assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: One who backs a horse is a punter, and one who backs a venture is a supporter.

clue.text: Gain attention without hesitation in trial

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the words in trial enclose the hesitation

parts.note: a test is a trial
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Getting noticed at a trial by speaking without faltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense of outside, so 'in trial' encloses the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone's curiosity is to capture their attention, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: King gets directions and is wiser

parts.note: Shakespeare's King Lear
N and S are compass directions, north and south

explanation.surface: A monarch receives instructions and becomes wiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear is the Shakespeare king who learns too late.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquiring knowledge makes someone wiser, so this verb means becoming so.
